Mechanical injury as a cause of cell damage

A man has extensive thigh trauma after being trapped beneath heavy machinery. Muscle fibers in the compressed region have disrupted membranes and release intracellular contents. Which category of initiating injury best fits the immediate local lesion?

  1. Physical injury with direct mechanical disruption
  2. Inherited absence of a lysosomal enzyme
  3. Excessive physiologic hormonal stimulation
  4. A primary autoimmune attack on intact muscle
  5. Deficiency of a dietary cofactor as the sole cause
Answer and explanation

Physical injury with direct mechanical disruption

Crushing directly damages cells; secondary ischemia can amplify that injury.

Option explanations

Physical injury with direct mechanical disruption: Crushing directly damages cells; secondary ischemia can amplify that injury.

Inherited absence of a lysosomal enzyme: A genetic storage disorder would not explain the acute localized trauma.

Excessive physiologic hormonal stimulation: Hormonal stimulation does not explain membrane rupture after compression.

A primary autoimmune attack on intact muscle: Autoimmunity is not needed to explain this traumatic lesion.

Deficiency of a dietary cofactor as the sole cause: A nutritional deficiency does not fit the immediate focal mechanical damage.
